vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawtrix-saas-intel
Version: 0.1.0

The clawtrix-saas-intel skill is designed to help agents discover relevant SaaS-focused skill bundles from clawhub.ai. It uses standard system tools (curl, jq) to query a search API and provides a scoring matrix for recommendations. The instructions in SKILL.md include explicit security warnings regarding the high risk of managing billing and authentication credentials, and no evidence of data exfiltration or malicious execution was found.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (finding SaaS-focused ClawHub skills) matches its instructions in broad strokes, but there are coherence gaps (undeclared dependencies, unclear personalization / data flow, and ambiguous sources for inputs) that you should resolve before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name and description align with the instructions: it searches ClawHub and outputs top-3 SaaS recommendations. However, the SKILL.md claims the results will be 'personalized to your product's domain, stack, and stage' but the provided search examples are static and don't show how SOUL.md content or agent-specific context is incorporated into queries. Also the file references commands (curl, jq, clawhub, clawtrix-security-audit) that are not declared as required binaries; that mismatch reduces clarity about what the skill actually needs to run.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly tell the agent to read the agent's SOUL.md and 'installed skills' and to write a report to memory. Reading SOUL.md is reasonable for discovery, but SKILL.md does not specify where SOUL.md lives, how installed-skills are enumerated, nor how to avoid sending potentially sensitive data (product internals, environment names, or PII) to external endpoints. The example curl queries are static and do not show how (or whether) agent-specific content from SOUL.md would be used in remote requests, creating ambiguity about potential data exfiltration risks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. That minimizes install-time risk (nothing is downloaded or written at install).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. It does note that SaaS agents often have access to Stripe keys and auth tokens, and recommends running a security audit, but it does not itself request any secrets. This is proportionate. Still, because it instructs reading SOUL.md and searching remotely, you should confirm the agent will not include secrets in external API queries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and is user-invocable. It writes output to an agent memory path (memory/reports/...), which is expected for a discovery/reporting skill and not excessive.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims, but there are gaps you should address before installing or running it in production: 1) Confirm the runtime environment provides the needed tools (curl, jq, the 'clawhub' CLI, and 'clawtrix-security-audit') or ask the author to declare them. 2) Ask the author to clarify how SOUL.md and installed-skills are discovered (paths, APIs) and to show exactly how product-specific data is incorporated into remote searches so you can audit what is sent out. 3) Ensure the agent will never include secrets (Stripe keys, auth tokens, customer PII) in outbound queries; prefer local parsing and redaction before any remote call. 4) If you will run this against real SaaS agents, test in a staging environment first and run the recommended security audit (or review its implementation) to verify it flags billing-access risks correctly. If the author provides a revised SKILL.md that (a) lists dependencies, (b) shows parameterized secure queries (no secret leakage), and (c) documents how SOUL.md is located, my confidence would increase to high and the skill would likely be judged benign.
